newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West spot power flat amid holiday slowdown.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West spot power flat amid holiday slowdown.

text.p: Spot power prices in the U.S. West were flat with most utility staffers off for the Columbus day holiday, market sources said Monday.
Next-day Palo Verde prices were unchanged at $19.25-19.75 per megawatt hour (MWh).
Next-day COB was also unchanged at $19.00 per MWh and Mid-Columbia was at $17.50.
"All the pre-scheduling for Tuesday was done last week. It was really quiet today," said one trader.
Spot prices were not expected to exhibit much change for the remainder of the week.
Traders cited the restart over the weekend of the 1,080 unit 2 at the San Onofre nuclear plant in California as putting a damper on the market.
In addition, temperatures in California and the Southwest are seen seasonally cool.
